sections.title: Interview bank U06: Training, adaptation, data pipelines

keyTerms.definition: Original practice, role-derived material. Not actual lab questions.
A set of breadth, ladder, analytical, debug, scenario, and critique questions per unit.

recall.question: What is the provenance of this interview bank?
recall.answer: Original practice, role-derived. The questions are not actual lab questions.

keyTerms.definition: Fitted power law: loss linear in log-log space vs scale.
Apparent jumps: usually a threshold artifact on a smooth ramp.
P(A beats B) = sigmoid(r_A - r_B).
W = W0 + (alpha/r)BA; r(d+k) trainable vs dk.

recall.question: Write the two-point scaling-law fit and the compute budget formula C = 6ND.
recall.answer: b = (log10 L2 - log10 L1)/(log10 N2 - log10 N1), L(N) = 10^(a + b log10 N). C = 6ND: 2N forward + 4N backward per token.

recall.question: Write the Bradley-Terry preference probability and the KL-regularized RL objective.
recall.answer: P(A beats B) = sigmoid(r_A - r_B). Objective: E[r] - beta * KL(policy || SFT).

recall.question: Write the LoRA update and its parameter count vs full fine-tuning.
recall.answer: W = W0 + (alpha/r)BA. Trainable: r(d+k) vs dk. Toy 4096/16: 131,072 vs 16,777,216 (128x).

keyTerms.definition: -0.0748 per decade on the toy fit.
Wins with exactly two runs and no visible floor.
Wins when large-N points bend flat.

recall.question: Deep ladder 1 fits a two-point scaling law: N1=1e9 L1=2.40, N2=1e10 L2=2.02. What is the fit and the N=1e11 prediction?
recall.answer: b = -0.0748/decade, a = 1.0534, L(1e11) = 1.70. Two points fix the line, so predict(N2) = L2 by construction.

keyTerms.definition: Scores responses from pairwise votes.
Penalizes distance from the SFT policy: E[r] - beta KL.
Reward climbs, human ratings fall; first fix: raise beta.

recall.question: Deep ladder 2 works the RLHF toy: r_A=1.2, r_B=0.8, KL=2.5, beta=0.1. What are P(A wins) and the objective?

keyTerms.definition: C = 6ND; doubling buys 0.301 decades of N.
Mean 2.31, std 0.0158 on the toy.
Gap under 1 std: no evidence; 2.5 std: evidence.

recall.question: C = 6ND with N=1e9, D=2e10. The budget doubles. How many decades of N, and what loss drop?
recall.answer: C = 1.2e20. Doubling buys log10(2) = 0.301 decades of N. Loss drops ~5% relative (factor 1.053).

recall.question: Seed sweep losses [2.31, 2.29, 2.33, 2.30, 2.32]. Recipe B reports 2.295, a third reports 2.27. Verdicts?
recall.answer: Mean 2.31, std 0.0158. B at 2.295: gap 0.015 < 1 std: no evidence. Third at 2.27: gap 2.5 std: evidence of a real win.

keyTerms.definition: Packed bins need a per-bin mask blocking cross-document attention.
Every query attends only within its own document.

recall.question: D1. The packing code fills bins but training diverges on long documents. What is the bug, the fix, and the invariant?
recall.answer: Bug: bins with no document mask, so attention leaks across packed documents. Fix: return (bins, masks) with a per-bin mask. Invariant: every query attends only within its own document.

keyTerms.definition: RLHF dominates; RLAIF keeps a niche for unlabelable rules.
Cost and loader levers die; packing, LoRA, scaling still matter.
Wins on simplicity when the preference set is fixed.

recall.question: Human labels are free and instant. Does RLAIF still have a role?
recall.answer: RLHF dominates on quality per label. RLAIF keeps a role only for rules humans cannot label consistently. DPO still wins on simplicity with a fixed preference set.

recall.question: The cluster price drops to zero but the power cap stays. Which U06 levers still matter?
recall.answer: Packing still matters (time-to-loss on real tokens), LoRA still matters (memory per task), scaling still matters. Cost-per-token and loader levers become irrelevant.

keyTerms.definition: Same eval? The 1B on an easier suite invalidates.
Threshold metric vs continuous score: the jump may be measurement.

recall.question: A paper claims “our 1B model matches a 10B model, so scaling laws are broken.” What five audit questions do you ask?
recall.answer: (1) Same eval? (2) Same data? (3) Same metric? (4) Cherry-picked tasks? (5) One seed?
